title: Jolt Physics: `intersect_shape` misses back faces on ConcavePolygonShape3D with `backface_collision` enabled.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.8.dev (39216f0c8da37d877241775ab35ad2cc5e3b837c)
- Reproducible in 4.7.3.rc (83dec14d549108e1f314f57c1ce7e932c65370dd)
- Not reproducible in 4.7.2.stable
- Regression from #120267 (cherry-picked for `4.7` in #123613)

### System information

Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (1920x1080 @ 165.00 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV PHOENIX) - AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 threads) - 60.60 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

On one of my test projects, I noticed a physics regression when going from 4.7.2.stable to 4.7.3.rc (83dec14d549108e1f314f57c1ce7e932c65370dd), where `intersect_shape` stopped reporting intersections with floors made of polygon shapes whose front faces are pointing downward. A sphere touches the back faces only (with `backface_collision` enabled) but no intersection is reported.

Looking at the changelog, #120267 seemed a potential culprit. Indeed, before that commit it would report the intersection twice (as per the bug report), and now it's 0.

I let an AI debug and propose a MRP, which is attached. TIWAGOS[^1], I haven't validated its claims on the cause nor the potential fix included in the MRP, what matters is whether the example shown in `main.gd` is indeed behaving wrongly.
